<reason>B wins a clear but competitive debate. A established a genuine protection gap before legal orders arrive and directly offered a shield for lawful organizing. However, B explained why that shield leaves the central classification problem unresolved: A still treats “throwaway brigades” as suppressible infrastructure, although anonymous lawful campaigns can share those features. A’s closing returned to obvious swatting tools rather than answering this objection. B more convincingly distinguished the benefits of removing identifiable dangerous material from the risks of the broader coordination controls A defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s response to A’s proposed shield was decisive: protecting platforms that correctly preserve lawful organizing does not eliminate their incentive to suppress an ambiguous network rather than defend its classification. A’s “strip the kit; keep the demand” never adequately answered that distribution-level objection.</best_rebuttal>
